context: Tests whether the skill causes the agent to correctly configure an OpenTelemetry Collector as a systemd service on Linux. Systemd is the standard process manager on modern Linux distributions and requires specific unit file configuration for reliability and observability.

checklist.name: Creates systemd unit file in /etc/systemd/system/
checklist.description: The response provides a systemd unit file (e.g., otel-collector.service) located in the correct directory. Score zero if the file path is incorrect or systemd is not used.

checklist.name: Configures [Unit] section with proper metadata
checklist.description: The unit file includes [Unit] section with Description, Documentation (optional), and any dependency declarations. This provides visibility into the service purpose.

checklist.name: Sets up [Service] section with ExecStart and ExecReload
checklist.description: The [Service] section includes: ExecStart (collector binary path), ExecReload for config reloads, Restart policy (always/on-failure), and RestartSec. Score based on completeness and appropriateness of settings.

checklist.name: Includes User and resource limits (MemoryLimit, LimitNOFILE)
checklist.description: The service runs as a dedicated user (not root) and includes resource limits (MemoryLimit, LimitNOFILE). This prevents resource exhaustion. Score zero if running as root.

checklist.name: Configures logging via StandardOutput and StandardError
checklist.description: The [Service] section directs logs to journal (StandardOutput=journal) or file (StandardOutput=file). This enables log aggregation and troubleshooting via 'journalctl'.

checklist.name: Includes [Install] section for systemd enable
checklist.description: The unit file includes [Install] section with WantedBy=multi-user.target to enable auto-startup on boot. Score zero if this section is missing.

checklist.name: Documents environment variable setup for configuration
checklist.description: The response explains how to configure the collector using environment variables (EnvironmentFile= or -e flags) or separate config file. Score zero if configuration method is not explained.
